items.title: Deadly Russian strike hits Odesa as von der Leyen arrives in Ukraine for defence talks
items.description: Russia carried out a strike on the port city of Odesa in Ukraine that killed three, a local official reported on Wednesday, as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Kyiv to announce new defence initiatives. Overnight, Ukraine also said it struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including gas…

items.title: US targets ICC in new offensive
items.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reopened a diplomatic campaign on Monday aimed at dismantling the ICC by combining sanctions, putting pressure on member states and seeking allies among major powers hostile to the institution.

items.title: How the 2016 coup attempt changed Turkey for good
items.description: Ten years ago, parts of the Turkish military attempted to overthrow the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The consequences of the failed coup continue to shape Turkey to this day. DW looks back.

items.title: Israeli strike on police post in north Gaza kills seven, officials say
items.description: A senior officer in the Hamas-run police force was among those killed in the strike, which Israel's military says targeted "terrorists".

items.title: Japan Admits Need to Counter Espionage After Russian ‘Den of Spies’ Report
items.description: The New York Times reported that thanks to "weak espionage laws," Moscow was using Japan as a hub for intelligence gathering and procurement of dual-use technology needed for its war in Ukraine.

items.title: ‘Hunted’ by drones: UN reports worst month for Ukraine’s civilians since 2022
items.description: Civilian casualties in Ukraine soared during the first half of 2026 amid escalating Russian attacks and intensifying use of deadly weapons, the UN human rights monitoring mission in the country, HRMMU, said on Tuesday.

items.title: Winter was harsh, but resilient Odesa making summer a season of hope
items.description: Odesa, home to a Ukrainian seaport that is a critical link in the global food security chain, endured its worst winter of Russian attacks since the war began, then prepared for a vibrant summer with a determination not just to survive but to build a better future.

items.title: The U.S. strikes Iran after Trump announces a renewed blockade and tolls in Hormuz
items.description: The U.S. and Iran are fighting for control of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a return to all-out war after agreeing to a ceasefire last month.

items.title: Zelenskyy Fights Another Political Battle With Another Cabinet Shake-Up In Ukraine
items.description: Zelenskyy gave no explanation for the unexpected shuffle of his Cabinet. But the popularity of Ukraine’s one-and-only wartime president is slipping, as war-weary voters tire of political scandals, as well as the unrelenting Russian invasion.

items.title: More Women Doing Dangerous Humanitarian Work
items.description: Women in Ukraine are increasingly taking on dangerous humanitarian roles, such as driving evacuation buses and delivering aid in frontline areas, as the four-year war steadily reduces the number of available male volunteers.
